requirement:
A record's `references` digest MUST be rewritten only if the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` current reference set of its subject,
under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`, has the recorded digest.
rationale:
**Obligations.** `requirements.refactor.reference_digest` has two parts:
1. A record's `references` digest is rewritten when the mapped-back current reference set of its subject has the recorded digest.
2. The digest is not rewritten when the mapped-back set has a different digest.

Mapped-back (`requirements.refactor.mapped_back`) means each new side of a mapping is replaced by its old side. The reference set follows `requirements.ci.reference_set`.

**Rewrite when the mapped-back set matches.**
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_function_keeps_its_evidence_current]` moves `fn[load]` to another file. Before the refactor, validation reports `fn[load]` as stale.
- The refactor then reports `evidence/rules.load.json` as changed.
- Afterwards `errors(root)` is empty. This shows the rewritten digest equals the digest recomputed for the new reference set.
- It also checks the record's input file, the rewritten rationale, and that other records are byte-identical.
- A second run reports `Changed 0 records`.
- A digest that was not mapped back would not match the recorded one. That implementation would block this move, and the test would catch it.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_file_rewrites_anchors_and_paths]` covers a file-level mapping that moves an `:impl:` anchor. It asserts that `rules.check` is rewritten and that validation is clean afterwards.

**No rewrite when the set differs.**
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_reference_set_changed_beyond_the_mapping_blocks_every_rewrite]` adds an `{impl}` that is not part of the move.
  - The report says "the reference set of core.load changed".
  - It does not report a text change.
  - The record file is byte-identical afterwards, so neither the text/input rewrite nor the digest is applied.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_changed_reference_set_is_reported_on_a_record_reading_nothing_moved]` is a record that has only a digest dependency on the move. An extra `{impl}` is added outside the mapping.
  - The report names `rules.check`.
  - The record is byte-identical afterwards.

**Conclusion.** An implementation that always rewrites, never rewrites, or skips the map-back step would fail at least one of these tests. The tests cover both outcomes with real assertions. Role changes and commentary edits would go through the same digest comparison as an added reference, so they are not a separate class. All four tests carry a `{test}` reference to the subject. I found no gap.

text: :::{req} reference_digest
A record's `references` digest MUST be rewritten only if the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` current reference set of its subject,
under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`, has the recorded digest.
:::{req} reference_set

A definition's reference set MUST consist of its current incoming `{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` edges, except a `{fixme}` inside a site of the definition under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles` and
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors`: for each edge, its role and the file and
outline selector of the node the reference belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, or of the anchored file or
node, and, for a fenced reference in a source outside the book, the words of
its body under the word rule of {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
`{cite}` references MUST NOT contribute. The reference-set digest MUST be
the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of those entries in sorted order,
so it does not depend on line numbers or on the order references are found.
For a structural assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_review`, the digest MUST additionally
include a versioned structural-assessment marker. A record predating structural
assessment MUST therefore be stale, including a legacy record with a wildcard
review version. Other assessments MUST retain their existing digest encoding.
Authoring MUST record the digest of the reference set it supplied, and
validation MUST recompute it and report a changed reference set as stale
evidence. Adding or removing an `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{fixme}` reference or anchor,
changing its role, editing its commentary, or moving it to a different node
MUST therefore make the evidence stale even when no recorded input changed; moving a reference within
the node it belongs to MUST NOT.
:::{definition} mapped_back
:phrase: mapped-back
The *mapped-back* form of current text or a current address is the text or
address with each new side of the mappings replaced by its old side.
